why: The criterion holds for all four verifier checks. Check 1 tests only values that "limited to the range lo to hi" requires: below the range gives lo, above gives hi, inside or on a bound gives x. That includes "clamp(7,3,3)", since the range 3 to 3 forces the answer 3. Check 2 only requires a RangeError when lo > hi, over three such inputs. Check 3 asks only that README.md documents each exported function ("its name with a description of what it does"). It does not require ### headings or exact wording, and the note that subtract must be documented follows directly from "every function". Check 4 requires only exit status 0 with no failing tests. The stricter items are all under "Advisory (not pass/fail conditions)": test coverage, the mutation test, the RangeError mention in the README and its message wording, and NaN behaviour. No check adds a branch or file-scope rule or an exact-wording requirement.
